newsitem.title: FRANCE: Some Elf workers extend strike, talks due - union.
newsitem.headline: Some Elf workers extend strike, talks due - union.

text.p: Oil workers at Elf Aquitaine's Grandpuits refinery near Paris voted on Monday to extend a five-day-old strike until Tuesday evening, an official with one of the unions involved in the protest said.
But talks have been arranged with managers for Tuesday afternoon at 1400 GMT, the official, from the CFTC union, said.
Workers at Grandpuits and two other refineries, Feyzin and Donges, had previously voted to continue their protest over job cuts and other demands until Tuesday morning.
There was no immediate word on whether Feyzin and Donges workers had also decided to extend their action beyond then.
Other union officials said the two plants were likely to follow Grandpuits' lead.

The strike has shut down virtually all Elf's domestic refinery production since last Wednesday and Thursday. Besides the three self-operated refineries, Elf has a 10-percent stake in the small Reichstett refinery in eastern France.
The three strike-hit refineries have combined distillation of 426,000 barrels per day -- 76 percent of Elf's total share of European refining capacity, according to its annual report.
